title: Capacity shadow run retrospective — Aug 25 2026
content:
Objective:
Run a shadow capacity sweep against canary fleet (us-west2) to repro the p95/p99 latency regression observed in production on 8/20 and trace root cause. Capture quota/backpressure effects when scaling from 16->64 concurrent generators, and compare behavior across model variants (gpt-ish-13b / gpt-ish-13b-quant) and cache temperature settings.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Reproduced increased p99 tail when moving concurrency above 32 for long sequence workloads (seq_len 1024–2048).
- Quantized variant shows slightly lower median latency but larger tail variance under mixed arrivals.
- KV-prefix cache warming is inconsistent: some workers show cold-streaming spikes even after 120s warmup; suspected race between cache population and worker reuse.
- Recent kernel-selection change (PR #1427 merged 2026-08-18) correlates with onset of production regression; likely related but not definitive.

Run details:
- Fleet: canary-us-west2 (dedicated pool, 8xA100 per node), runtime image: rwinference/runtime:2026-08-18-kerndefault
- Model variants: gpt-ish-13b (fp16), gpt-ish-13b-quant (4bit), model file hashes noted in run logs
- Workload: mixed traffic generator (prompt mix A/B/C), skew: 60% short (seq<=256), 30% medium (512), 10% long (1024-2048)
- Concurrency levels: 16, 32, 48, 64 (steady-state for 10 minutes each)
- Batch configurations: dynamic-batch=on, max-batch-tokens=4096, batch-window-ms=10
- KV cache temp: cold (0s prefill), warm(120s prefill), sticky (prefill + keepalive 300s)
- Observability captured: per-token latency traces, worker-level heap stats, GPU utilization, PCIe Tx/Rx, network egress, runtime thread dumps every 30s

Key numbers (selected):
- Baseline (concurrency 16, warm cache): p50 28ms, p95 82ms, p99 190ms, throughput 12k tokens/s
- Regression point (concurrency 48, warm cache): p50 33ms, p95 210ms, p99 680ms, throughput 28k tokens/s (token/s increases but latency tail degrades)
- Quant variant (concurrency 48, warm cache): p50 27ms, p95 260ms, p99 980ms (higher tail variance)
- Cold-cache long seq (concurrency 32): p99 spikes >2s on ~3% of requests

Observed anomalies and clues:
1) Worker-level mismatch: some workers show persistent high CPU steal and delayed NVLink transfers coincident with tail spikes. Candidates: kernel fallback path increases CPU involvement, or scheduler starvation from background maintenance tasks.
2) Cache population race: trace shows prefix entries created but not immediately visible to subsequent requests handled by a different worker process. This leads to repeated cold fills and repeated KV-store replication.
3) Batch packing pattern shifts: under mixed arrival, batch compositions skew to single-large-request batches, causing longer per-batch GPU kernels and increased queuing. This is worse for quant variant due to different kernel latency shapes.
4) GC/heap churn: runtimes with older glibc allocator show transient heap pauses coinciding with p99 spikes. We saw correlation with container image variant x.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A. Kernel-selection PR #1427 introduced a fallback that runs a CPU-side copy path for certain seq lengths, causing periodic CPU-NVLink handoffs and tail increase.
B. Worker reuse policy + async cache write propagation causes transient cache misses for requests routed to recently-reused workers.
C. Batch window heuristics interact badly with mixed arrivals, producing inefficient batch packing and longer head-of-line times for some requests.
D. Container image variant (malloc/allocator differences) yields GC-like pauses on hot workers.

Experiments to validate (next week):
- Reproduce with runtime image pinned to 2026-08-11 (pre-PR1427) and compare.
  owner: Ravi Patel, due: 2026-08-28
- Flip worker reuse to 'no-reuse' for 1h to see cache warm behavior and measure p99.
  owner: Evelyn Park, due: 2026-08-27
- Run synthetic arrival shaping to force homogeneous batches and measure tail under same concurrency.
  owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-08-27
- Swap allocator to tcmalloc variant in canary for subset of workers to gauge heap pause effects.
  owner: Sofia Martinez, due: 2026-08-29

Short-term mitigations suggested:
- Lower max-concurrency per node for long-seq routes to 32 until we confirm root cause; add autoscaler override to reduce burst capacity for those routes.
- Add guardrail: if p99 > 500ms for long-seq for >2m, route to fallback model variant with sticky cache prefill.

Notes on telemetry & missing signals:
- Need per-request kernel-id tagging in traces to attribute which kernel path executed on GPU (missing now).
- Per-worker NVLink queue depth instrumentation would help disambiguate PCIe/NVLink stalls.
- We lack cross-worker cache-coherency metrics (time between write and next-read visibility). Adding this to KV-store telemetry should be prioritized.

Meeting attendees / who was present:
Maya Chen (note-taker), Ravi Patel, Evelyn Park, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Martinez, Jun Wei (SRE), Hannah Lee (observability)

Action items (short list):
- A1: Pin runtime to 2026-08-11 for 2h run and collect traces (Ravi) — 2026-08-28
- A2: Run no-worker-reuse test for warm prefills (Evelyn) — 2026-08-27
- A3: Implement temporary autoscaler override for long-seq routes (SRE) — Jun Wei — 2026-08-26
- A4: Add kernel-id tagging to tracing SDK (observability infra) — Hannah Lee — 2026-09-03
- A5: Draft post-mortem template if regression reaches customer impact threshold (Maya) — 2026-08-30

Open questions / discussion points:
- Is quant variant acceptable as a short-term fallback option given higher p95/p99 variance? (product input needed)
- Can we tolerate slightly lower throughput for long-seq routes in exchange for improved p99? (cost trade-offs)
- Is there a rollout rollback policy for kernel-selection PRs that can be invoked faster?

Appendix: useful commands / snippets used in the run:
- start generator: ./tools/traffic-gen --mix profile-A --concurrency 48 --seq 1024 --duration 600 --target canary-us-west2
- collect traces: ./infra/trace-collector --fleet canary-us-west2 --since 2026-08-24T22:00Z --out traces/aug25
- compare latencies: ./scripts/latency-compare.py --baseline images/2026-08-11.json --candidate images/2026-08-18.json --metric p99

Comments / notes to self (informal):
- This felt messier than previous regressions because the system still shows improved throughput while tail latency degrades — ie it's not an obvious slowdown but a variance issue. Keep pressure on getting kernel-level observability to avoid wild goose chases.
- We should add a small non-production test that simulates cross-worker cache miss behavior to validate the race quickly.

End of notes.
summary: Shadow capacity sweep reproduced p99 tail regressions above concurrency 32 on long sequences; cache warming race and kernel fallback are top suspects; set of experiments and short-term mitigations proposed.
